questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom/phrase.

Throw in the towel

options.text: To cause an activity or process to continue
To take responsibility for a situation while another person is temporarily absent

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Throw in the towel"** means to give up or surrender, especially after a struggle or when facing defeat. (हार मान लेना)

 
 
• **Example:** After failing the exam multiple times, he decided to throw in the towel and pursue a different career path.
 
 
 
• **"Surrender"** refers to the act of yielding or giving up in a situation, especially when facing overwhelming opposition. (आत्मसमर्पण करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The soldiers had to surrender when they were surrounded by the enemy troops.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "Throw in the towel" aligns with the concept of giving up or surrendering.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: To prepare to fight** (लड़ाई के लिए तैयारी करना): This means gearing up or getting ready for a confrontation or challenge.

 
 
• **Example:** The boxer started preparing to fight as he entered the ring.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To cause an activity or process to continue** (किसी गतिविधि या प्रक्रिया को जारी रखना): This means ensuring that something progresses or does not stop.
 
 
• **Example:** He worked tirelessly to cause the project to continue despite the challenges.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To take responsibility for a situation while another person is temporarily absent** (किसी व्यक्ति के अनुपस्थित होने पर स्थिति की जिम्मेदारी लेना): This refers to stepping in to manage something temporarily in someone else's absence.
 
 
• **Example:** She agreed to take responsibility for the team while the manager was on leave.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Whoever got the __few__ answers correct has to leave the room.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **fewest**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"few"** means a small number of things or people. It is used to describe a countable quantity. (थोड़ा या कम संख्या में)

 
 
• **Example:** Only a few students attended the class today.
 
 
 
• **"Fewest"** is the superlative form of "few" and is used to indicate the smallest number in comparison to others. (सबसे कम संख्या)
 
 
• **Example:** Among all the players, John scored the fewest goals this season.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "Whoever got the few answers correct has to leave the room," the use of "fewest" is correct because it denotes the smallest number of correct answers in comparison to others.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Fewer** (कम): Used to indicate a smaller number but not the smallest in comparison.

 
 
• **Example:** There are fewer cars on the road during weekends.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: More fewer** (अधिक कम): This is grammatically incorrect because "fewer" cannot be preceded by "more." The correct usage would be either "more" or "fewer," depending on the context.
 
• **Option 4: Most few** (सबसे कम): This is incorrect because "most few" is not a proper grammatical construction. Instead, the superlative form "fewest" should be used.
 
• **Option 5: Few** (थोड़ा): Refers to a small, indefinite number but not in a comparative or superlative sense.
 
 
• **Example:** A few people came to the meeting despite the rain.

**Complete Sentence:** *The professor delivered a complex__ lecture on quantum physics.*

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The car which I bought last year was cheap than my bike.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. was cheap than my bike .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase **"was cheap than my bike."**
 
• The word **"cheap"** is a comparative adjective, and it must be followed by **"than."**
 
• However, the correct comparative form should use **"cheaper than"** instead of **"cheap than."**

Correct sentence: *The car which I bought last year was **cheaper than** my bike.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Comparative Adjectives:**

 
 
• Comparative adjectives are used to compare two things.
 
• They often end with **"-er"** (e.g., bigger, cheaper, faster) or use **"more"** for longer adjectives (e.g., more beautiful, more intelligent).
 
• The word **"than"** is used to introduce the second item being compared.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• This house is **bigger than** that one.
 
• She is **more intelligent than** her brother.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which was landing at 5:00 a.m. yesterday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. flight which was landing .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "flight which was landing" is incorrect because the verb "was landing" implies an ongoing action, which does not fit the context of a completed event in the past.
 
• The correct phrase should be "flight which landed," as it accurately describes a past event.
 
• Using the past continuous tense ("was landing") here creates a grammatical inconsistency in the sentence.

Correct sentence: *My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which landed at 5:00 a.m. yesterday*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + was/were + verb (ing).
 
• **Example:** The plane was landing when it started to rain.
 
• **Usage: **Describes ongoing actions in the past that were interrupted by another action.
 
 
 
• **Simple Past Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Subject + verb (past form).
 
• **Example: **The plane landed safely.
 
• **Usage: **Refers to completed actions in the past.
 
 
</ul
